title: CEO Interview with Daisuke Okanohara of Matlantis
gist: Matlantis CEO Daisuke Okanohara describes a cloud atomistic simulator built on PFP, a universal machine-learning interatomic potential covering 96 elements and running up to 10 million times faster than DFT, used by 150+ organizations. He highlights growing semiconductor process use (ALD/ALE, HF etching of SiO2), trust/IP concerns from customer surveys, and a push to let non-coding chemists run simulations via AI agents such as Claude Code and the Case Studio tool.

insights.claim: Matlantis's PFP universal machine-learning interatomic potential, developed by Preferred Networks, covers all 96 elements from hydrogen to curium in one model and runs calculations up to 10 million times faster than density functional theory (DFT).
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: ML potentials collapse materials-simulation time, shifting value from HPC compute toward AI-native simulation platforms.
insights.quote: One model covers all 96 elements from hydrogen to curium, and it runs calculations up to 10 million times faster than DFT.

insights.claim: Matlantis began in 2021 as a joint venture of Preferred Networks and ENEOS with Mitsubishi Corporation investing, and R&D teams at more than 150 companies, universities and institutions now use it, including Volkswagen and Hyundai Motor Company.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Gauge of industrial adoption of AI materials simulation across autos and energy.
insights.locator: We started in 2021 as a joint venture

themes.theme: R&D bottleneck: simulation time and trust

insights.claim: In a Matlantis survey of 300 US materials scientists and engineers, 94% said their team had abandoned at least one project in the past year because simulations ran out of time or compute.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quantifies latent demand for faster simulation tools and compute in materials R&D.
insights.quote: 94% said their team had abandoned at least one project in the past year because simulations ran out of time or compute.
insights.locator: Last year, we surveyed 300 U.S. materials scientists

insights.claim: Only 14% of surveyed materials scientists felt very confident in the accuracy of AI-driven simulation, and every team raised concerns about protecting IP in cloud tools, making trust and data security the key adoption barriers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vendors that win validation benchmarks and security certifications (e.g., ISO 27001/27017) should gain share in AI-for-science.
insights.quote: only 14% of respondents felt very confident in the accuracy of AI-driven simulation
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Okanohara frames simulation access as having three barriers — infrastructure, science and scripting — with cloud delivery solving infrastructure and AI agents targeting scripting so experimental chemists can compute without code.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI agents expand the addressable user base of scientific software beyond scarce computational chemists.

insights.claim: At Matlantis's annual user conference, nearly 70% of respondents said they use AI for simulation and calculation and about 38% now tackle calculations that were previously impractical.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Evidence that AI-accelerated simulation is moving into mainstream industrial R&D workflows.
insights.locator: Matlantis is delivered as a cloud service

insights.claim: Semiconductor process development is a growing focus for Matlantis because atomic-scale surface reactions in deposition and etching are very hard to observe in the lab; semiconductor users include SCREEN and Resonac.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI atomistic simulation is becoming a tool in ALD/ALE precursor and process development for chip materials suppliers.

insights.claim: Using PFP with GRRM20 reaction-path search on a ~200-atom slab (vs a ~20-atom cluster in earlier DFT work), Matlantis completed a full search of a cobalt ALD precursor reacting with hydrogen-terminated Si(111) in about a week, showing how a ligand change lowers activation energy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Enables precursor screening for area-selective deposition, relevant to materials suppliers for advanced nodes.
insights.locator: In ALD and ALE, Matlantis helps

insights.claim: A LightPFP simulation of SiO2 dry etching fired 1,000 HF molecules at a ~72,000-atom slab, opening etch holes over 2 nm deep within about 500 ps of simulated time with reaction pathways matching DFT-level accuracy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Large-scale ML simulation of etch chemistry could shorten etch process development cycles.
insights.locator: In another published case, we used LightPFP

insights.claim: ENEOS used PFP with NVIDIA ALCHEMI to evaluate about 100 million candidate structures for oxygen evolution reaction catalysts, cutting discovery from years to months.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows Nvidia's push into AI-for-materials workloads and GPU demand from scientific simulation.
insights.locator: On the catalyst side, ENEOS used PFP

insights.claim: Matlantis customers typically compare it with conventional DFT codes, open-source universal MLIPs and in-house models; Okanohara sees DFT as the complementary accuracy reference and says open-source MLIPs have improved quickly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Open-source MLIP progress is a commoditization risk for proprietary potentials; differentiation shifts to service and validation.
insights.locator: Customers usually compare us with three options

insights.claim: Matlantis's PFP v9 tied for first overall on MLIP Arena, an open benchmark testing whether ML interatomic potentials behave realistically in practical simulations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Benchmark leadership supports Matlantis's accuracy claims versus open-source rivals.

insights.claim: Matlantis differentiates on cloud delivery with no customer compute infrastructure plus direct support from its materials and computational chemistry team in Tokyo and Cambridge, alongside tools like LightPFP, GRRM20 and Matlantis CSP.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Service-plus-model bundling is the moat thesis for AI-for-science SaaS.
insights.locator: Third is the support around the model

insights.claim: Matlantis released a public Skills library on GitHub teaching general-purpose AI agents to run its simulations, and an installer lets customers launch agents such as Anthropic's Claude Code from the Matlantis terminal so researchers can describe simulations in plain language.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Example of coding agents becoming the interface to domain-specific scientific software.
insights.locator: This spring, we released a public Skills library

insights.claim: Matlantis Case Studio, co-developed with Resonac, lets experimental chemists customize existing cases through AI dialogue with no programming; across four demonstration rounds non-specialists completed calculations on first use, with an alpha release coming.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: No-code AI interfaces could widen Matlantis's user base inside chemical companies.
insights.locator: In September, we announced Matlantis Case Studio

insights.claim: Matlantis is scaling throughput with NVIDIA ALCHEMI and launched Matlantis CSP in January to find previously unknown stable crystal structures.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Crystal structure prediction is a growing AI-for-materials category tied to GPU compute.
insights.locator: We’re also scaling throughput with NVIDIA ALCHEMI
